synopsis: Time-history agreement compares complete simulated and measured curves to expose timing and shape differences that peak-only checks miss; for automatic braking, identical peak deceleration can still produce different collision outcomes [f14739, f7783]. The booklet’s FAA example shows 0.3% peak error but 60.4% time-history error, whereas another example has 3.42% peak error and 7.2% time-history error, both within that example’s 10% guideline; these are aviation examples, not stated heavy-machine acceptance thresholds [f7785, f7782, f7764]. The proposed heavy-machine program should validate the entire chain from detection through brake-pressure build-up to deceleration, speed and position, including distance-to-object and relative-speed histories near the collision boundary, using multiple agreement metrics rather than one score [f7786, f7787, f8042]. Available methods include Sprague-Geers magnitude-and-phase comparison and ISO 18571’s corridor, phase, magnitude and slope rating; the glossary identifies ISO 18571 use in a 2026 automatic-braking/proving-ground demonstration [f7763, f15332, f14745]. Cross-chapter sensor evidence also includes Haider et al.’s time-domain and point-cloud validation, dated October 2022 in Chapter 6 and associated with an August 2023 publication in Chapter 10, but both accounts identify the evidence as on-road [f4505, f7819].
